e-9112.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance of a Scaled Random Variable
e-9112.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = 2.3,$ calculate $\textrm{Var}[-10X].$ 

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.5$ |
e-9112.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\textrm{Var}[aX] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-10.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[-10X] & =(-10)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =100\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\textrm E [X] =2.3.$ 

We start by computing $\textrm E[X^2].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X^2$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =1(0.2)+4(0.3)+9(0.5) \\  & =5.9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5.9-{(2.3)}^{2} \\  & =0.61.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[-10X] & =100\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =100\cdot 0.61 \\  & =61.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9114.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance of a Transformed Random Variable
e-9114.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\textrm{Var}[aX+b] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-2$ and $b=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[1-2X] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =4\cdot 10 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=-\frac{1}{2},$ calculate $\text{Var}[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}X].$ 

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |
after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}X] & ={(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=-\frac{1}{2}.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot f(-2)+(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{2})+1(\frac{1}{8})+1(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{13}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{4}-{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{4}-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}X] & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 3 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-7$ and $b=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[1-7X] & =(-7)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =49\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=3.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}+4\cdot \frac{2}{7}+16\cdot \frac{4}{7} \\  & =\frac{73}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{73}{7}-{3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{10}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[1-7X] & =49\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =49\cdot \frac{10}{7} \\  & =70.\end{aligned}

The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=3,$ calculate $\text{Var}[1-7X].$

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[1-7X] & =(-7)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =49\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}+4\cdot \frac{2}{7}+16\cdot \frac{4}{7} \\  & =\frac{73}{7}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}

$$
